title: Dispatch: Opus-review repairs batch G (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch G for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8, from the adversarial Opus review bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.14 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.14`; read S34 (reopened, combatant side), S35, S36, S37, S38, S39, S40 in full, each with a registry repro). Lifecycle design: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.10` (D1-D9). Keep every lifecycle rule inside nextCombatantLifecycle (D1).

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS:
D2 REVERSED (closes S40 structurally, SRD rule:healing: a creature that has died can't regain hit points until magic restores it to life): a dead combatant stays dead in BOTH death-rule modes; positive hpDelta and non-'dead' explicit statuses on a dead combatant are refused. No revival operation exists in this PR. Update the I8 invariant/comments, the transition matrix rows, the combatant tests that asserted monster revival (replace with the refusal), and the update_combatant description ("a dead combatant cannot be healed" for both modes). Monster suffocation still kills (monster default) and needs no block because death is now terminal.
S34 (combatant): resolveCombatantDeathSave (encounterCombatants.ts ~2098) must arm the seeded recovery schedule whenever the transition result is stable, including the zero-effective-max natural-20 third success; route the schedule through the same path as an ordinary third success. Registry test: PC goblin 1/1, adjust_exhaustion 4, saves 12, 12, 20 → stable with a schedule; then advance_time settles per D5.
S35: under monster rules, damage to a combatant at 0 HP (unconscious from a knockout) kills it (main's behaviour; rule:stabilizing-a-creature / monsters die at 0). Critical or not. Fix combatantLifecycle.ts (~274) and the matrix row at combatantLifecycle.test.ts (~700).
S36: a dying player-character combatant's turn is AVAILABLE for its start-of-turn death save, like a character's: begin_turn must not auto-complete a dying combatant's turn, so record_death_save can run at the start of that turn; end-of-turn effects (hydra regrowth) settle when its turn actually ends (the next begin_turn). Stable/unconscious/dead stay unavailable as today. Update the begin_turn description to state this. Registry test reproducing the review's hydra sequence: the save is recorded before regrowth; with two failures banked a failed save kills it before any regrowth.
S38: admitting/projecting a monster-rules campaign actor that is unconscious at 0 HP (knocked out) keeps it unconscious at 0 HP and leaves the canonical actor unchanged (main behaviour); only real terminal causes make it dead. Registry test through close and start_encounter.
S37 (nit, accepted): set_surprised description: when creatures on both sides are hiding, call set_surprised once per side, each with the passive comparisons for that side's hiders against the other side's observers. Add a registry test for the both-sides case through two calls.
S39 (nit, accepted): record_death_save and stabilize_character descriptions (combatant parameter): combatant death saves and stabilization happen only during the combatant's active combat instance; a dying player-character actor whose encounter closed continues its death saves when it is next brought into an encounter. No behaviour change.

Each fix with a generalized regression through the tool registry where model-facing. Run `npm run verify:worktree` before the final commit; commit; record a completion report (files, each finding → test names, any deviation, verify result) with `bd update <your bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <your bead>`. Do not push, open a PR, or modify any other bead.
acceptance_criteria: Listed findings repaired with generalized regressions; D2 reversed; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the agent.
